item.title: Seeking review: Furry Clinic.
item.description: A bullied person makes a clinic that turns people into their fursona counterparts
item.content:encoded:
A bullied person makes a clinic that turns people into their fursona counterparts, permanantly, and painfully, you won't be able to mingle in society.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Alright I think I can write a decent article this time, this would be my 5th attempt at a concept being approved, although I thought of many more I scrapped. So, yeah, a furry, gets bullied in his childhood so he decides to become a furry, and thinks that: "Every furry I know wants to be their character! I'll find a way to make this come true!" He experiments a while to finally make a clinic which anyone who enters comes out their fursona. Non-furries find it exceptionally hard to locate. Now a side affect of this surgery is well, the subjects immediately seek out the nearest furry, and try to force them in, once they do so, the subject will return to the place they last slept, and wake up with no memory of this, I intended to make the creator of the clinic realize what he had done, he had ripped families apart, because he thought he was helping them, in reality, he didn't.

item.title: SCP Idea "Thunder"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Happy(?)

Page Layout: Standard article with a death report and psychological analysis, and maybe a interview log

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block

•The SCP consists of two parts, POI-628356 and SCP-XXXX

•SCP-XXXX Is a dog formerly named "Thunder", who was previously owned by the POI-628356. According to the article, POI-628356 is the 15 year old son of A Researcher at a random site (Still haven't decided) who, as mentioned above, owned SCP-XXXX

•SCP-XXXX had to be put down at a vet clinic due to complications from a brain tumor.

•The SCP itself is anomalous because despite being "Dead" It still exists and acts like a completely normal dog. It eats, poops, pees, drinks and can even be petted. However, The SCP is completely invisible to everyone Except POI-628356 and other dogs.

•The whole concept behind the SCP is the fact that despite being dead, SCP-XXXX is in a quite literal sense, always with The Person of interest. This article is more about the story than the SCP.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

The Central narrative follows the aftermath of Thunder's death and the effect it has on POI-628356, as well as the results of seeing his dog "alive" again. The Psychological analysis and vet clinic report will be the main focus of the article, with the possible interview log between POI-628356 being a sort of closing addition to how much thunder meant to POI-628356 and how happy he is to be able to see his dog again, even if no one else can.


Hook/Attention-Grabber:
+ show block
– hide block

The Article is meant to be a happy and sad SCP article, and is mainly to play into the idea that "They're only gone if you think they are" In a literal sense.

item.title: SCP idea: Retroactive weight gain supplement
item.description: A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but
item.content:encoded:
A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but it actually rewrites your memories to make you only think you have lost weight. Use it too much and your memories start getting weird.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Edit: Added the required template.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Page starts with basic containment procedures and a description. The main part of the narrative will be in the experiment log, which will reveal more about the effects of the SCP and may include interview logs with the test subjects.

Elevator Pitch: A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but it actually rewrites your memories to make you only think you have lost weight. Use it too much and your memories start getting weird.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP is a weight loss pill that you can order a subscription to though an anomalous phone number. Each pill rewrites your memories a little bit to make you believe you lost weight after taking the pill. Since it does not actually cause weight loss in the present, you probably will actually gain weight without knowing it. The more pills that are taken the fatter you will believe you used to be and the further back in time it changes your memories. Eventually, you will be convinced that you have been morbidly obese your entire life before you started taking the pills. If you keep taking the pills past this point (I will call this the critical point for now), things start to get strange. The boxes that the pills come in have two languages on them. One is English (or whatever language you speak) and is all lies, and the other is an unknown language. After the critical point, you gain the ability to read the unknown language, which tells the truth about what the pills do, and you start to gain memories from before you were born of being something not human.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is a weight loss pill that retroactively turns users into gluttony monsters in human form, or at least makes them think they are.

Additional Notes: I haven't decided yet how much it affects other people's memories or physical records like pictures. I haven't decided yet what happens if you stop taking the pills, though it probably depends on if you have passed the critical point or not. I may end up leaving it ambiguous if it is actually changing the past or just your memories.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Safe class SCP: The Wrong Chair
item.description: a chair that is impossible to remain seated in
item.content:encoded:
The wrong chair is a chair that is impossible to remain seated in due to discomfort. If one remains seated anyway nearly harmless anomalous effects may occur.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Other (Simply a strange object)

Page Layout (Optional): Standard Format

Elevator Pitch: This is a chair, bench, or other form of seating that makes anyone that tries to sit there very uncomfortable with the idea of sitting there without any physical effects. It is not possible to contain, however, as it relocates via unknown means.

Central Narrative: The Wrong Chair almost always replaces damaged seating in seemingly random locations around the planet. It also has no uniformed appearance. Occasionally it will appear as an additional seat in a room instead of replacing a broken one. The Wrong Chair causes minor psychological distress to those seated on it until they move, but there is no lasting effects upon standing. If anyone manages to remain seated for more than 2 minutes and 37 seconds The Wrong Chair will disappear, leaving them to fall to the ground, or to land on top of the damaged seating The Wrong Chair formerly replaced. The Wrong Chair will always relocate within 24 hours, and always appears somewhere unobserved. In at least two cases it appeared when someone blinked, replacing a broken seat in the room they were in. ETC.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Simply enough this is just something bizarre but mostly harmless, yet impossible to contain.

Additional Notes: First try by me! People told me to submit the idea here from other locations.

item.title: Dr Cheese SCP-5672 idea.
item.description: The proposal for SCP-5672 I have made. It sucks, I know. Its my first SCP.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Like most SCP articles, it is structured by Item Name, Class, SCP, description then the addendum. Unlike some, I have not included a picture in my article. One may be added, but this is unlikely. Information about the anomaly's origins come first, then descriptions of it and what it is, followed by their strengths, weaknesses and abilities.

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is a trio of skeletons labelled A,B and C. Each one has a different anomalous ability, being teleportation of matter, telepathic brainwave reading and matter configuration. They all have 3 things in common. They are six (6) foot (2) inches and weigh twenty-seven (27) pounds. The other common feature shared is that despite being composed of normal human bone composition (Collagen and Calcium Phosphate) they are extremely indestructible, except to electricity ranging from two thousand to four thousand (2000-4000) volts.
This incapacitates the entities, therefore tesla gates are positioned outside their containment cells. Safe/Euclid classification is an ongoing decision as they seem to use their abilities for the good of the world, but this could just be a publicity stunt to trick the foundation.

Central Narrative: The Story with these anomalies is that they were found in a cave in outer London, and DNA tests suggests they were part of the royal family in 15th century Britain.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There isn't much special about the premise of SCP-5672 apart from the anomalies abilities, which were thought to be obtained by strange minerals and substances in a cave under London.

Additional Notes: Caesium-135 and Strontium-99 were found in small traces near the cave entrance. This suggests prolonged exposure to radioactive material, but no nuclear bomb/accident has occurred in the UK.

item.title: The Phantom
item.description: A cat-like apparition that consumes souls.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Class, containment procedures, a professional description of the SCP and what it does, followed by three incident reports.

Elevator Pitch: Put simply, SCP-XXXX is a cat-like apparition which consumes souls. It once had intangibility (Which it lost during an incident), and it can shield itself from all wavelengths of light, rendering itself invisible for a short duration.

It’s a hunter, so it stalks any kind of prey which catches its interest, though it prefers humans. It will stalk its target, memorizing all of its routines, mannerisms, and daily patterns in extreme detail. When they are at a point of vulnerability (Provided SCP-XXXX hasn’t lost interest) it will consume their soul.

After a large amount of souls are consumed, it exhales them into the form of a polychromatic sphere, which it then carries to an unidentifiable and unspecified location.

+ Show block
- Hide block

That’s how it’s going to be written, but in actuality, SCP-XXXX is bringing the sphere to a GOI (Of my creation) so they can use it to prevent some kind of cataclysmic event from occuring. The Foundation is unaware of this, and all they know is that whenever they try to take the sphere away from the SCP, several events occur:

  1. SCP-XXXX becomes extremely agitated.
  2. People start disappearing from the Foundation (They’re actually being dragged away by a hand of the SCP which actually causes the cataclysmic event.)
  3. Emergence of multiple anomalous entities appearing all over the world
  4. Cataclysmic event occurs.

Central Narrative: It’s a question of morals. The Foundation has to escort SCP outside after it creates the sphere (Which can even be a problem at times), but each time it’s outside it also does what it wants, and consumes even more souls. Even though the SCP’s job is presumably important, is it morally correct for the Foundation to just let it go around killing people?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Since the SCP has lost its intangibility and is now at odds with the Foundation, this prompts it to use its superior intelligence to resist and counteract any new containment procedures that the Foundation tries to come up with.

Additional Notes: Last time I left out a lot of details, since I was trying to summarize way too much. Hopefully this is a good balance of things. Once again, any advice is highly appreciated, and thanks in advance.

item.title: A video game that kills you (seeking greenlight)
item.description: A video game that kills anyone who played it...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • The SCP is a video game cartridge with scratched up stickers and scratched logo and title which is impossible to make out.
  • a video game cartridge that can be played on Nintendo 64, but no one1 remembers or knows about the game or the development of the game.
  • whenever a player dies in the video game, within 24 hours the player in real life would face the same fate as the player who died in the video game.

Central Narrative:
The whole idea of this SCP is that the game kills the subject the way the subject died in the video game.

When the cartridge is plugged into a regular Nintendo 64, the player will be introduced into an open-world. The place that sets the player in a city called: "Alt City", the player inside the game can virtually do ANYTHING2. The more the player plays in the city, the more the player wants to commit violence.

Whenever the player dies in the game then the tv unknowingly shuts off with no solutions fixing it. Within 24 hours the player will die in real life in the same way the player died in the game. There is no other way of avoiding death, and any attempts avoiding the death would just lead to death.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is special about this SCP is because I think (I THINK! I am not certain) that this SCP is the first video game that kills anyone. (Again, I am not certain, there is probably an SCP like this. I don't know…)

Additional Notes: I would LOVE to see some criticism or feedback. Thank you!

Footnotes
1. as in people in a video game developing companies, as well as Nintendo
2. in that, they can commit any crime easily

item.title: SCP-IDEA (MITTERNACHTSONNE) 2nd ATTEMPT
item.description: IGNORE ME [thread locked, repeat]
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Horror
Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX commonly called (Midnight sun) is a:
⦁ Large 45 m dark quadrupedal aquatic life form
⦁ Similar in appearance to the prehistoric lizard known as mosasaurs
⦁ Has a Tentacle mane around the back of cranium
⦁ Travels at speeds equal or in access of 400km/h
⦁ Strength to body to ratio is 20:1
⦁ Covered in Robust Black scale armour exterior
⦁ It Can only viewed at night
⦁ Avoid direct eye contact, avoid viewing for more than 1 minute continuously
⦁ It's origins remain unknown
⦁ Was on the move until it was contained at the THE RING
⦁ Can increase area of influence

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
SCP was first alerted to the foundation through an agent located in NOAA(National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration), NOAA noticed a drastic change in salinity in area 1km2 somewhere in the Atlantic. Initial expedition failed resulting in the loss of all life. Data emitted during time of expedition discovered: salinity in the water had changed and that the underwater local flora/fauna had mutated and become highly aggressive, SCP causing this was found to be also extremely aggressive and intelligent. SCP was contained at the site known as the THE RING after 3 failed expedition and considerable loss of life. Containment was achieved with the aide of new countermeasure technology such as: PUVDS ( perimeter ultra violet defence system- a defence systems which emits a strong ultra violet light deep into the water)- pinning SCP into a confined area, SPS( Sea perimeter system- a system designed to prevent the influence of SCP-XXXX from exceeding a 20km2 zone and for the salinity of water to not change outside of the zone. Loss of life was deemed acceptable to contain SCP-XXXX given its aggressiveness and intelligence and usual parameters of containment failing. SCP-XXXX full name is Leviathan der Mitternachtsonne (Leviathan of the Midnight sun) and was named by a formerly deceased Kreigsmarine U-boat/K version captain.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP most dangerous ability is that it is capable of salinity conversion, which if left uncheck can cause cataclysmic change in weather, flora/fauna, disrupt oxygen levels. SCP-XXXX is also capable Phycological Physical Mutation (Able to transform a victim using their brain to mutate their body, without the need of physical contact provided certain conditions are met) creating 5 sub entities of various forms like the Gespenst(wraith). It uses this ability to great effect in order to escape its confinement.

Additional Notes: Constructive criticism is greatly appreciated.👍

Elevator Pitch: The premise is that there was a dragon and a phoenix (who both have humanoid forms) were lovers a long time ago the male is the only one who remembers and protects the female through each time she dies and is reincarnated having no memories of her previous life. Usually leading them to fall back in love. The male dislikes humans and has destroyed civilizations that have harmed/kill the female. The female loves all life and always tries to stop the male from hurting anyone.

Central Narrative: The main story part of the article would be about the foundation trying to contain the Male/Female SCP. This has multiple outcomes based on how the foundation goes about containment through each incarnation of the female. Example The foundation tries to just take the female and keep her locked up against her will leading the male to attack the site to free her, or they convince the female to come willingly and use her to contain the male which sometimes has an ok outcome. The male is immune to most forms of physical harm and can even nullify other SCPs anomalous effects if it is to protect the female or himself. The foundation becomes interested in containing the male to help contain other SCP because of his ability to nullify other effects. The male will not always just do what the female says and will even go against her wishes if he feels like he is protecting her.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The attention grabber is an ancient dragon protecting his phoenix lover that does not remember him after she dies. His raw power making containment of him or her near impossible.

Additional Notes: This is my first time writing an SCP so any feedback or advice would be appreciated.

item.title: The Railyard To Everywhere
item.description: An interdimensional railyard with goods from across dimensions being transported and sorted through it.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery, Horror

Elevator Pitch: The SCP (from now on referred to as the railyard) is a 1km x 300m railyard found in a pocket dimension. It is only accessible by a junction located a few miles from the Southeastern entrance of the Bradway Tunnel in South Yorkshire. Inside the yard, there are about 50 sidings and 14 entryways (9 of which lead to tunnels) and two operating facilities. Surrounding the yard is a rocky, heathland similar to those found in the UK.

On some occasion, locomotives enter the railyard via the tunnels or junctions. Locomotives of all kinds will enter and exit the railyard and will only remain to dispatch/pick up all cargo. The only locomotives permanently found within are a GWR 9400 Class and two BR Class 10.

Central Narrative: The junction was initially found in 1965 during the Beeching Axe. Reports came in of workers vanishing when they attempted to find the end of the line. The Foundation came in when a BR DMU went missing along with 37 passengers.

Across numerous expeditions, the foundation makes a number of bizarre discoveries. During one expedition, the foundation attempted to remove some of the wagon's contents. Upon doing this, the shunters became very hostile toward the personnel and attempted to prevent them from escaping the railyard. Two personnel died in the escape.

In the penultimate log, it mentions a 'smoke' engine exiting the junction, with four humans on board. Later, during an interview with one of the humans, she reveals to be one of the passengers who went missing on the BR DMU a few years before. During her interview, she described the world she and her fellow passengers were in and what they did in order to return to their reality.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: During one expedition, a 5AT1 came into the railyard and dropped off mail van. Upon inspection of mail, the foundation discovered that most of the mail was in written in Nguni languages and some had post dates of 31st of June and 32nd of October. These discoveries caused the foundation to deduce that the railyard not only connects alternative dimensions but also parallel universes.

Additional Notes: I will not do anything related to Thomas & Friends!

Footnotes
1. A steam engine only proposed in our word

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) Aquí Hubo Escena
item.description: Memetic agent that affects songs.
item.content:encoded:
Memetic agent that affects songs. you either get a positive or a negative effect based on your perception of said song.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Page Layout: Looking to use a format similar to those of SCP-4028, SCP-3020 and SCP-3031. Audio files if possible.

Elevator Pitch: A memetic agent starts spreading across finished musical compositions. Depending on the fame, the listener's perception and the themes the piece touches, this agent can cause all sorts of benefitial or detrimental changes on a person's body and psyche. Although the agent starts propagating on niche music spheres, it eventually reaches mainstream hits.

Central Narrative: Trough different evidence we learn about our PoI, an anomalous individual who was heavily involved in his country's music scene. In naive attempt to improve his situation and the one of his fellow companions, he ends up risking up the veil and getting the community he so much loved killed (both metaphorically and literally). After barely surviving lynching and escaping persecution, he releases the memetic agent with ambiguous motivations.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Aside from the fact this skip deals with a not so explored topic, this entry has the intent of confronting the Foundation with a fundamental dilemma: is it really better to live on your knees than to die on your feet? Is the Foundation really willing to declare a war on artistic expression for the greater good?.

Additional Notes: It's Intended to be a connection between our PoI and the GoI "Deer College", this may change in the future.

item.title: Echos eines Hoffest
item.description: A city returns to medieval times for a day. Foundation intervenes and it becomes permanent.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): History

Page Layout (Optional): Video logs, interviews, document references and incident logs to be included.

Elevator Pitch: The city of Mainz (Germany) gathers annually during the Pentecost day for a party in which the citizens anomalously change their behaviour as if they were in the 12th century for a day. After an incident, the Foundation intervenes only to provoke this change to become permanent.

Central Narrative: During the Pentecost day in Mainz, its citizens celebrate the festivity in a nearby location, where upon access they show an altered behaviour proper of the European nobility in the 12th century, such as a firm code of honour; and participate in joust tournaments. By the following day, citizens involved have no related memories.

+ Show
- Hide

Recordings posted in an online video-sharing platform alerted Foundation about these effects. A task force bursts into the gathering, disbanding all attendants. This time affected individuals keep their memories and the behaviour displayed during this event. Chaos ensues due to the cultural clash with modern Germany.

The next Pentecost day, affected population gathers again, live-recordings showing that the activities performed are exactly the same as in the previous year. Once the celebration finishes, all attendants return to the normal behaviour. Foundation decides not to interrupt this event, but stops population from attending by fencing the site. Instead, attendants move to nearby Ingelheim, where anomalous natural catastrophes result in hundreds of casualties. The Foundation allows the event to occur at the usual location.

Recording logs interview seemingly a monk, who seems to be responsible of these events. Back in 1184, Kaiser Barbarossa hosted a huge fest in that same location. By law, Konrad was to be seated by the Kaiser during the ceremonies, however he was substituted in a political move by the Archbishop of Cologne. Resentful, he condemned the dishonour, ensuring that that day would be repeated over and over until the Kaiser rectified his mistake.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is a story about timely cultural clash, by bringing a huge population from the past to the current days. It is also a story about resentment and, literally, holding a grudge.

Additional Notes: Based on the 1184 Mainzer Hoftag. Kaiser Barbarossa might be SCP-125-DE.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a phenomenon where an abnormal number of crows migrate directly to the town, even if it off-tracks their intended migration path.

More
Not more

The highest amount of crows in the town was 84,784.

When a house in the town is damaged, it will start to heal itself, although minor damages take less time to heal. Damages won't be healed as an identical version of the house such as doors leading to nothing, rooms or objects with an irregular shape, etc.

A unique crow will be "assigned" to a specific house. These crows are distinguishable by their single white feather. These crows will interact with the occupants of the homes.

The foundation discovered that when a crow is killed, the house's self-repairing is assigned to stops entirely.

Central Narrative: The narrative is presented in a personal journal belonging to a young teenage girl named Sahra.

more
not more

Their crow comes to their house. He's Chip because he brought a chip as a gift.

The large and irregular migration of crows to the town is detected by the locals. The town tries to find a way to scare off the crows. But it doesn't work, as every time one crow leaves, more come in.

Sarah's dad one day breaks a door hinge while slamming a door shut. He later calls one of his friends to help fix it when he gets back home, but it's fixed when they return home.

Soon the crows outnumber the town's population 31:1.

Everyone tries to scare off the crows. They use fireworks, predators, big hunting, but none of them work because every time one goes away, more come to replace it. Soon the crow's number in the thousands.

A car crashes into Sarah's house and kills chip. The damaged part attempts to repair and starts to start to expand and use wrong materials. The crow's brain went on overdrive before dying. This was when the foundation was informed.

The foundation came, amnesticize everybody, and found Sarah's journal.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An article with a light story isn't as common as Lovecraftian horror and Apollyon class SCPs.

Additional Notes: Sarah and her family were in the first instance of SCP-XXXX which is why the foundation hadn't known about the anomaly. also had to put the bare minimum in the narrative because of the word limit.

item.title: Psychological Theories in 1800s
item.description: For a therapy SCP who was originally trained in the 1800s, what theories and practices would they most likely adhere to had they been trained around this time?
item.content:encoded:
This SCP is a reality-affecting entity that was captured by an English Earl (or baron, I'm unsure) at some point in the 1800s, probably around 1850 or later. I think the upper limit should probably be 1900 when the British nobility was dying off.

The earl in question had an interest in Psychology, and when he captured the anomalous entity he realised it's potential to help cure his patients. He slowly reformed the entity over time to genuinely come to enjoy helping humans, and it continued when he died.

A problem is is that the SCP mostly focuses on Therapeutic techniques, which from what i can gather came about more when Freud entered onto the scene, which i think was 1880 or so, which is a little early i think. It is also set in Britain, so it would be whatever theories were popular there.

So I'm currently unsure what theories of treatment this entity may subscribe to, as it would depend on which theories were around when it was being trained under this earl.

item.title: De Facto
item.description: An octopus that exploits laws of reality to actively shape the environment however it sees fit.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror

Elevator Pitch: De Facto is an intangible entity that can descend upon any location and transmute it to develop anomalous properties. It presents cephalopodic features and primarily resides outside of our reality, traveling freely along or through any surface and molding the environment into its personal hunting grounds.

+ Show More
Hide Section

Central Narrative: This creature was originally a rare variant of octopi possessing intelligence that far surpasses humans held in a secret underground marine biology laboratory. Its kind can adapt to the environment very quickly but are critically endangered due to human pollution and influence. The cephalopod retains a grudge over transgressions of its captors. When it eventually learned it could adapt into its surroundings and extend beyond the third dimension, the intelligent animal gruesomely tortured and slaughtered every member of personnel and fled to the surface for more prey.

Whenever the creature possesses any structure or area with indeterminate range, it twists and warps it with ecological abominations that can only reflect the deepest, darkest depths of the ocean floor where human eyes never dare venture. It populates these areas with incredibly distorted and mutated marine life to kill any non-marine life, capable of moving and breathing as though they were in the water. It transmutes surfaces with ink-coated rocky surfaces, capable of completely restructuring any architectural layout for its horrors to easily chase prey into deadly traps set by the cephalopod itself, if the beasts don’t devour them first. The subject descends on areas or structures often inhabited by humans, feeding on them either for sustenance or sport.

The Foundation was informed of this fiend’s presence when police reported homes in Tampa, Florida undergoing sudden and dramatic anomalous changes, with the original residents going missing afterward. It’s intangibility and ability to pass through any surface makes it impossible to contain, however assigned Foundation personnel can track its movements and minimize risk of death by detecting locations currently occupied by the anomaly. All attempts to directly seize and capture the being result in complete massacre, only remains being staff personal logs and communication devices. It does this intentionally, so listeners know that they’ll be next, someday.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An intangible entity can transform any building or location into the deepest, darkest ocean depths, populating it with ecological horrors bent on exterminating all surface dwellers.

item.title: I'd Rather Be Part of the Serpent's Hand Than the Foundation"
item.description: I would be going, "SCREW THE FOUNDATION, YO! DOWN WITH THOSE GOSHDARN JAILORS!"
item.content:encoded:
So, I think the Serpent's Hand would be better to be a part of / work for than the SCP Foundation. Here are all my points, in no particular order:

1. Foundation operates out of boringly-decorated, overly sanitary-looking research facilities filled with deadly monsters that can get loose at any second, not to mention they are constantly raided by the Chaos Insurgency. The Serpent's Hand gets a frikin' extradimensional library that requires actual frikin' magic to access, and is actually very safe because all of the anomalies within are friendly as long as nobody gets violent against them or breaks the rules. Nice place to chill and relax, maybe play some Dungeons and Dragons and write in peace.

2. Foundation deprives anomalous humans of their humanity, and instead locks them up in basically prison (I don't give a crap about how much you think Iris Thompson likes it there, she most likely secretly hates being locked up, along with literally any other human SCP).

3. They fight for the rights of law-abiding anomalous humans that just want to go about their lives without having to worry about being either imprisonated by the SCP Foundation, murdered by the Global Occult Coalition, weaponized by the Chaos Insurgency, or sold by MC&D. Basically, they tell everybody else to chill their heels and leave anomalous people the heck alone. Which is actually a pretty noble cause. The only reason they raid Foundation / GoC locations is because that is one of the only ways to get their points across. Plus, they do stealth missions, and kill Foundation personnel in only a limited capacity.

+ show block
– hide block

4. The Serpent's Hand doesn't breach dangerous anomalies for no good reason at all. That's the Chaos Insurgency's job, after all. If the Serpent's Hand doesn't have a good reason to breach any given SCP during a raid, they won't breach said SCP. They do, however, steal Safe SCP items, and let peaceful human SCPs to escape. They may even attempt to free D-class if possible. They're not stupid, and they don't want to bring about the end of the world by releasing highly dangerous Euclid, Keter, and Apollyon SCPs. Again, that is the Chaos Insurgency's job.

5. Simply existing as a worker on a Foundation site means that you are alive on moment, and then the next you are dead due to being freakin' eaten by a massive lizard that is literally too angry to die or turned into a zombie by a dude cosplaying as a medieval plague doctor, and your friends and family will be unaware of your death (if all of them are outside of the foundation, which is most likely). If you do manage to survive through the containment breach, you will still be mentally scarred by the experience. As I said earlier, the Serpent's Hand operates out of a peaceful library, with a 0% chance of being eaten by a bloodthirsty monster.

6. I also believe that the serpent's hand probably is one of the morally better GoIs, considering their entire mission statement is "we want rights for anomalous humans, and knowledge about the paranormal should be public." While they do break the law from time to time (which would make them Chaotic or Neutral Good), they don't do so for no reason at all. They just want the world to be a better place.

item.title: The Drag Strip Phantom / The Black Magnum [Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
An SCP heavily and very directly inspired by Christine, The Wraith, Death Proof and SLR:Redline.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Thriller

Page Layout (Optional): Standard description and event chronology as well as mission reports and test logs

Elevator Pitch: The phantom of a car that manifests itself on lonely stretches of desert road at night to challenge high-performance passer-by cars to a drag race. Original manifestation is 1970 Camaro, however the list will expand later.

Central Narrative: A rumor spreads in a small town in Colorado about a mysterious "ghost car", originating from a local drag racing enthusiast. According to the legend, the racer is overtaken by a dragster and the road eventually leads into a foggy, abandoned drag strip - with a stoplight and everything. The Foundation takes note after several others report the same occurence and dispatches a team to study the anomaly up-close and personal ("prodding" the car during manifestations and exploring the strip dimension), as well as launching an investigation into the car's possible origins.

+ show block
– hide block

At one point, a GoI destroys it with a rocket launcher. A week later the phantom manifests in the closest town and has a brief run-in with a used car salesman while stealing a new muscle car. The Foundation attempts to contain the phantom following its rediscovery, as well as manage new cases of the SCP cropping up. In addition, the original phantom has now gained an apparent interest in humans.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The mystery surrounding the car itself: Is it sentient, is it dangerous, what is the drag strip, is/was it a real place, where does the car come from, is there anyone driving it, what is its driving force etc. etc. Later on, the phantoms' interactions with humans.

Additional Notes: The drag strip is a separate dimension that renders back-and-forth communication impossible./Cars cannot leave the dimension unless they engage in the race or get totaled./Anyone who dies on the strip in a car becomes another manifestation./The phantoms are free to switch or modify their vessels./Phantoms all have a physical form as their previous selves' corpses./If a phantom's manifestation is "killed", a new one will appear after some time, depending on the damage./Each phantom is sentient and remembers its entire "afterlife"./Phantoms have little to no memory of their past lives./The SCP can manifest at will anytime between sunset and dawn./It is not bound to any road in particular and can move at any time.

Elevator Pitch:A simple bronze statue, 3 meters in height, with an emotionless, nondescript face. The statue, each day of the year, produces an object that is laid at the feet of the statue. This object can vary, from a blank book, a briefcase of money, or a gun. The way this object is used depends on the weather, therefore creating an infinite amount of possibilities for what could happen, with global warming and greenhouse gases. The statue also sometimes goes into a "bad" mood, with the item that is produced being used against the person picking it up, for example, a handgun produced at the feet of the statue could have the safety off and be fully loaded, giving a chance for the person picking it up to shoot themselves if they are not careful.

item.title: Matter altering SCP
item.description: A machine which can transform atoms to given molecules or other atoms
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Scientific

Elevator Pitch: A giant block of gold was found in an abandoned Soviet Cold War era laboratory. After X raying it some human bones and a giant machine were present inside. It was noticed that it was turned on aswell because of the sound it was emmiting, so it could function without any power supply.

The main concept of this SCP is that it can alter the structure of atoms and it can make bond between those atoms that are present to make molecules. Basically it can convert air to gold or dust to super medicine. It has a few settings detailed “crystals”, “powder”, “liquid”, “gas”, “biological”. The buttons are labeled in languages of the nations that were the part of the Soviet block and the Warsaw Pact.
Experiments are going to be held with this machinery given SCP qualification. (This means that I will think about the most odd things that I can bring out of this)

Central Narrative: It will be a document among researchers and doctors. I will need to create dialogs and experiment logs. I would also take suggestions from you and try to succesfully implement them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Thinking of making this into a thaumiel SCP because it can help out the foundation by a lot if it is in the good hands because it can help create amnestics or chemicals needed there.
If it is held in the wrong hands it can end the world in many ways like crashing the economy or creating weapons of mass destruction or if we look at the biological setting it can make anomalous entities.

Additional Notes: Well I know that this scp sounds like the combination of the coffee machine and the old steampunk gear machine but I will try my best to make a uniqe SCP and take this concept to a whole new level.
Also if you know any SCPs that are too similiar to this please notify me and if you don’t like this at all I will scrap the idea this is just the basic concept that I have posted and there will be a lot more to this.

Just an extra information: I’m a chemist and this topic is really close to my heart.
